title: Same-stage naturality and descent of a scalar-compatible rational point family
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. All coefficient fields below are finite intermediate extensions of $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings and uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $g:s\to s$ be a scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\mathcal C_E^{\rm int}=D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $\mathcal C_E=D^b_c(s,E)$, the raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $P_E=Lg_E^*$ with its specified integral, rational and common-stage actions [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $F_E^{\rm int}=\Gamma(s,-)$ and $F_E=\operatorname{Fib}_s:\mathcal C_E\to D^b_{\rm fd}(E)$ be the specified point-section functors [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and put $H_E=F_EP_E$.

For $E\subseteq L$, write $S_{L/E}K=K\otimes_E L$ for rational scalar extension and $T_{L/E}A=A\otimes_E L$ on point complexes [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. Let $\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}:S_{L/E}P_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_LS_{L/E}K$ and $\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}:F_LS_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E}F_EK$ be precisely the rationalizations of the specified completed pullback and sections comparisons [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Define
$$b_{E,L,K}=\bar\varphi_{E,L,P_EK}\circ F_L(\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}^{-1}):H_LS_{L/E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E}H_EK.$$

Suppose that, for every finite $E$, maps $t_{E,K}:F_EK\to H_EK$ form a natural transformation on $\mathcal C_E$, and suppose they satisfy
$$b_{E,L,K}t_{L,S_{L/E}K}=T_{L/E}(t_{E,K})\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}.$$
Assume the unit and tower equations for $b$ with the specified source and point-complex associators, and that for a representative $u:S_{L/E}K\to S_{L/E'}K'$ the two specified common-stage functor actions are represented by
$$A_L(u)=\bar\varphi_{E',L,K'}F_L(u)\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}^{-1},\qquad B_L(u)=b_{E',L,K'}H_L(u)b_{E,L,K}^{-1},$$
with scalar transport of these arrows equal to the corresponding formulas at every larger field. Use the literal common-stage source and target categories [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. Put $t^L_{E,K}=T_{L/E}(t_{E,K})$, with the prescribed unit identifications when $L=E$.

For every representative $u$ the equation
$$B_L(u)t^L_{E,K}=t^L_{E',K'}A_L(u)$$
holds in $D(L)$ over that very same $L$. Applying $-\otimes_L N$ and the source and target associators to this equality gives the equality for $u_N$ for every finite $N\supseteq L$. If $[L,u]=[L',v]$, then at some common finite $N$ their transported equations have identical left and right sides. Consequently the finite-stage classes $[E,t_{E,K}]$ define a natural transformation $\operatorname{Fib}_s\Rightarrow\operatorname{Fib}_s\circ Lg^*$ with these components and this same-stage naturality. There is no requirement that the maps $t_{E,K}$ be isomorphisms, that coefficient transitions on morphisms be injective, or that the rational family have an integral lift.

source.place: Deligne, Weil II, (1.1.3), p. 150; (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 gives the point-transport context only. Original coefficient-descent proof steps 6-7: naturality in D(L) and representative independence by extension to a common field. The completed pro-etale normalization and explicit formulas are an agent-written argument, not assertions attributed to Deligne.

proof.text:
Fix $L\supseteq E,E'$ and write $X=S_{L/E}K$, $Y=S_{L/E'}K'$, $t_X=t_{L,X}$, $t_Y=t_{L,Y}$, $\varphi=\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}$, $\varphi'=\bar\varphi_{E',L,K'}$, $b=b_{E,L,K}$ and $b'=b_{E',L,K'}$. The assumed scalar equations say $t^L_{E,K}=bt_X\varphi^{-1}$ and $t^L_{E',K'}=b't_Y(\varphi')^{-1}$. Naturality of the supplied transformation $t_L$ at the actual arrow $u:X\to Y$ says $H_L(u)t_X=t_YF_L(u)$. Substitution and cancellation give, entirely in $D(L)$,
$$B_L(u)t^L_{E,K}=b'H_L(u)b^{-1}bt_X\varphi^{-1}=b'H_L(u)t_X\varphi^{-1}=b't_YF_L(u)\varphi^{-1}=t^L_{E',K'}A_L(u).$$
Only the comparison isomorphisms were inverted; neither $t_X$ nor $t_Y$ was inverted.

proof.text: For $N\supseteq L$ put $U=T_{N/L}$ and use the target associators $c$ of [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. For each endpoint $(E,K)$ let $c_F:T_{N/L}T_{L/E}F_EK\to T_{N/E}F_EK$ and $c_H:T_{N/L}T_{L/E}H_EK\to T_{N/E}H_EK$ be their components, with primes at $(E',K')$. Naturality of $c$ at the morphism $t_{E,K}$ gives $c_HU(t^L_{E,K})c_F^{-1}=t^N_{E,K}$, and likewise at the other endpoint. The assumed scalar transport of the two functor actions gives $c_F'U(A_L(u))c_F^{-1}=A_N(u_N)$ and $c_H'U(B_L(u))c_H^{-1}=B_N(u_N)$, where $u_N$ uses the prescribed source associators. Apply the functor $U$ to Step 1, postcompose with $c_H'$ and precompose with $c_F^{-1}$. Inserting $c_H^{-1}c_H$ and $(c_F')^{-1}c_F'$ gives exactly $B_N(u_N)t^N_{E,K}=t^N_{E',K'}A_N(u_N)$. This also covers $N=L$ by the unit equations.

proof.text: If $[L,u]=[L',v]$ in the literal source category, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] gives some finite $N\supseteq L,L'$ with $u_N=v_N$ as arrows between the same extended endpoints. Step 2 takes both equations to this $N$. The two equations now have left sides $B_N(u_N)t^N_{E,K}$ and $B_N(v_N)t^N_{E,K}$, which are identical, and right sides $t^N_{E',K'}A_N(u_N)$ and $t^N_{E',K'}A_N(v_N)$, which are identical. By the target equality rule in [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category] these represent the same equality of morphism classes. No implication from equality at $N$ back to equality at $L$ or $L'$ is used.

proof.text: At the object $(E,K)$ take the component $[E,t_{E,K}]$, using the prescribed unit identifications. More explicitly its representative between $T_{E/E}F_EK$ and $T_{E/E}H_EK$ is $\iota_{E,H_EK}^{-1}t_{E,K}\iota_{E,F_EK}$. The transition formula and naturality of the tower and unit isomorphisms in [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category] identify its representative at $L$ with $t^L_{E,K}$. Composition of classes is composition at a common field by that same definition. Thus for any $[L,u]$ the naturality square of these components is represented by precisely the two composites in Step 1; those composites are equal over $L$. Step 3 makes this independent of its representative. Components and this square for every arrow are the data of the required natural transformation between the two specified functors. The argument used only the supplied rational family and functor laws; it requires no integral lift and no injectivity of transition maps.
